scope: Engineering live-browser pre-UAT before requester acceptance

checks.evidence: Home identifies the unofficial prototype, beer, wine, distilled spirits, one-product intake, batch intake, and the 500-record history boundary.
The built-in two-panel sample completed without manual data entry and returned distilled spirits with high confidence, 24 checks, and 19 matches.
Brand, class, 45 percent ABV, 90 proof, 750 mL, producer and address, and the beverage rule profile were visible with clear machine states.
Show on label selected the original-pixel brand polygon, panel number, OCR text, and label-derived comparison boundary.
Warning inspection displayed the prescribed statement, all 43 observed words, 9 matching subchecks, the source panel crop, and physical size as not applicable from a photograph.
Table, Cards, and Image first layouts were selectable and reported their checked state.
Keyboard help exposed optional shortcuts for disposition, exceptions, check movement, panels, warning inspection, and closing.
History retained the completed sample with images, type, machine result, disposition, filtering controls, newest-first paging, and the 500-record FIFO statement.

A four-image batch showed a live processed counter, progress bar, current image, elapsed time, 5.3-second running average, 11.4 images per minute, estimated time remaining, and zero isolated failures.

The grouping screen displayed three suggested products, one or two images per group, the three-image limit, confidence and conflict explanations, merge and split controls, per-group confirmation, and a locked Run action until confirmation.

automatedCoverage: Beer, wine, distilled spirits, unknown, and conflicting rule profiles
Batch retry, cancellation, exports, and 300-product capacity
History update, delete, clear, browser-scope isolation, and FIFO eviction
Oversized browser-decodable image preparation and server-side limit guidance
Responsive, keyboard, focus, and accessibility behavior
limitations: The requester acceptance signature remains open.
Private image uploads were not repeated during the browser pre-UAT because the commit-bound release gate already processed the governed and private corpora.
Technical execution and observable OCR output do not replace agency legal-label acceptance.
